name: Laver Of Brass
overview: The Laver of Brass, also called the Brazen Sea, was a significant brass basin crafted by Solomon for the temple, as described in 1 Kings 7:23-26. It was a large, round basin, supported by twelve oxen facing the four directions, and adorned with intricate floral designs. Positioned in the temple courtyard between the altar and the tabernacle, it was used for ceremonial washing, symbolizing purification before approaching the altar or entering the tabernacle. This laver, made from the brazen mirrors of the women and anointed with holy oil, points to Christ as the fountain for sin and the necessity of regeneration before consecration.
